To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Indian cuisine is characterized by a strong signature of ‘negative food pairing’, i.e. the extent of flavor similarity between any two ingredients is negatively correlated with their co-occurrences in a cuisine, which is not explained by recipe size or ingredient category based recipe constitution.

(i) the Indian cuisine has a distinct pattern of negative food pairing that is not explained by the ingredient category-based recipe composition; and (ii) ingredient frequency and spice usage are dominant factors that shape recipe composition in the cuisine.
Indian cuisine has a characteristic flavor sharing pattern, which is independent of recipe constitution and is dominated by the frequency of ingredients.
